questions.solution:
Calcium phosphate is the major component of hydroxyapatite crystal that form the inorganic portion of the teeth

questions.q: The difference between electron gain enthalpies will be maximum between :
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Electron gain enthalpy is defined as the amount of energy released when an electron is added to an isolated gaseous atom. During the addition of an electron, energy can either be released or absorbed. Electron gain enthalpy decreases down the group because as we move down the group, the size of an element increases, and the effective nuclear charge decreases. Due to this, the incoming electron will experience less attraction. Thus, electron gain enthalpy decreases as we move down the group.

ΔHeg for chlorine=-349 kJ mole-1

ΔHeg for Neon=+116 kJ mole-1

ΔHeg for Argon =+96 kJmol-1

ΔHeg for fluorine =-333 kJ mol-1

questions.solution:
Correct order of bond dissociation enthalpy of halogens is Cl2>Br2>F2>I2.

questions.q:
Choose the correct statements from the following

A. All group 16 elements form oxides of general formula EO2 and EO3 where E=S, Se, Te and Po. Both the types of oxides are acidic in nature.

B. TeO2 is an oxidising agent while SO2 is reducing in nature.

C. The reducing property decreases from H2S to H2Te down the group.

D. The ozone molecule contains five lone pairs of electrons.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
(A) All group 16 elements form oxides of the EO2 and EO3 type where E=S, Se, Te or Po. And these oxides produces acids on hydrolysis.

(B) SO2 is reducing while TeO2 is an oxidising agent. An oxidising agent is a substance that causes oxidation by accepting electrons; therefore, it gets reduced. A reducing agent is a substance that causes reduction by losing electrons; therefore, it gets oxidised.

(C) The reducing property increases from H2S to H2Te down the group. This is because the bond energy E-H(E=S,Se,Te) bond decreases down the group.

(D)  have six lone pairs

questions.q: Anomalous behaviour of oxygen is due to its
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Due to its small size, Oxygen exhibits high electronegativity, a high charge/ radius ratio, and no d-orbital oxygen shows anomalous behaviour.

Oxygen exists as a diatomic molecule as O2 comprising a double bond whereas all the other elements of group 16 exist as polyatomic molecules.

Oxygen is paramagnetic and exists in a gaseous state at room temperature, which is completely opposite of the other Group 16 elements.

The small size and high electronegativity of Oxygen enable it in the formation of pπ-pπ multiple bonds.

All the given elements belong to the group - 18. All noble gases have general electronic configuration ns2np6 except helium which has 1s2. Since noble gases have stable electronic configuration, they have no tendency to accept the electron and therefore, have large positive values of electron gain enthalpy.

Values of electron gain enthalpy of all the elements are given in the below table

Element ΔegH[KJ/mol]
He +48
Ne +116
Kr +96
Xe +77

So, the order is He < Xe < Kr < Ne.

questions.subject: Chemistry

As noble gases do not form compounds, hence they cannot occur in the form of diatomic molecules. 

Noble gases, being monoatomic, have no interatomic forces except weak dispersion forces and therefore, they are liquefied at very low temperatures. Hence, they have low boiling points.

Noble gases are held together by weak dispersion forces.

questions.q:
The number of inter halogens from the following having square pyramidal structure is

ClF3, IF7, BrF5, BrF3, I2Cl6, IF5, ClF, ClF5
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Square pyramidal structures are BrF5,IF5 and ClF5.

These molecules are made up of 6 equally spaced sp3d2 hybrid orbitals arranged at 90o angles. The shape of the orbitals is octahedral. One orbital contains a lone pair of electrons, so the remaining five atoms connected to the central atom gives the molecule a square pyramidal shape. Among the given options the structure with five bond pairs and one lone pair is these three structures only.
